reachable: Yes, and verified by execution rather than reading. At the scoring layout (L = 2r+1, read command at index 2r, its observation absent) the pointer channel contributes to the scored prediction: driving ptr_gate.bias to -60 changes the read-position prediction by mean |delta| 0.0031, max 0.0145, against a prediction magnitude of 0.481 — about 0.6% at init, and the gate/readout are both trainable. The read at step i uses memory written only by steps < i (mem starts at zeros, writes at step i land on columns <= i, and the mixture carries an explicit (j < i) mask), so nothing about the withheld answer is required. Causality confirmed numerically: perturbing obs_{r-1} by 100x moves only command r's prediction (all earlier command positions change by exactly 0.0), and one read row in the recurrence carries 1.08e-6 at its own index, right at the 1e-6 floor the author declared, which the explicit mask then removes. Gradient reaches the mechanism in training: after one backward, grad norms are addr_proj.weight 4.3e-3, ptr_out.weight 2.8e-2, ptr_gate.weight 2.1e-3, ptr_move.weight 1.6e-4, ptr_erase.weight 1.3e-5 — all nonzero. The one starved parameter is ptr_log_sharp (5.4e-7, and displacement-capped at ~1.33 over the budget), which is the second divergence above. Occlusion is live within the budget: the smoothstep ramp gives p=0 at step 300, 0.0066 at 400, 0.060 at 650, 0.113 at 900, 0.120 from 1000 on, against a 4000-step default budget; eval-mode forward is bit-identical across calls and occlusion-free. A short synthetic 80-step optimisation is numerically stable (no NaN, loss falls to 3.3e-3).
solves_outside_model: No. This is clean on the axis that has previously been abused. The whole file consumes only tok_emb, types and key_pad; there is no import of the pack, no access to `cmds`, no string parsing, no path normalisation, no chain resolution in Python. `cmd_raw = tok_emb[:, 0::2, :]` is a slice of the model's own input, `_role_addresses` is a coordinate-block slice + soft threshold + one shared nn.Linear, and the whole routing is a torch recurrence (`_pointer_route`) over those addresses whose gradient the model owns. Which content ends where after a chain is never computed anywhere but inside that recurrence. The one thing worth naming explicitly: the arch hard-codes the genome's stream layout (src_lo=0/src_hi=352, dst_lo=352/dst_hi=704, matching r3_srcdst_hashslot_coding's SRC_LO/HI and DST_LO/HI exactly). That is co-design against a fixed slice of the model's input, i.e. ordinary architecture, not a resolved answer arriving at the input — the stream stamps each command's OWN src/dst path identity, which is information the command string already carries at scoring time, and it is separately covered by the read-token-parity invariant on the stream axis. No head/arch/batcher/target shape of the prior retraction is present here.
summary: The implementation is a faithful, careful build of the mechanism it describes — the recurrence matches the hypothesis's equations line for line, the occlusion half is a verbatim port of r22_observation_occlusion_denoising, inherited parameters are bit-identical to the parent at init, the mechanism is reachable and gets gradient at the scored read, causality is exact, and nothing resolves routing outside the model. Where it diverges is on its headline CAPABILITY claim. "Depth-invariant composition — the surviving pointer is as sharp as after one hop" is true only for the idealised address set the author simulated (mutually near-orthogonal unit vectors, which I reproduce as depth-flat at mass 1.000 for depths 1-6). Composing the author's own two offline sims — running the real `_pointer_route` on addresses that the real `_role_addresses` produces from the genome's real stream codes, with ideal gates — the pointer's hit rate on the true origin drops from 57% at depth 1 to 20-23% at depths 3 and 4 with 8 slots, i.e. it degrades with depth precisely on the eligible slice, which is the regime the proposal exists to win. The stated remedy compounds this: the learned power exponent inits at 1.0025 through a softplus(-6.0) whose Jacobian is 0.0025, and AdamW over this genome's schedule can move the raw parameter at most ~1.33, capping the exponent at ~1.01 out of [1,4] — so the sharpening that would re-concentrate mass (I measured depth-4 hit rate 23% -> 43% when the exponent is forced to 4) cannot engage during a scored run. The MEASURED numbers the author reported without torch are otherwise honest: the addressing cosines reproduce inside their stated error bars (theta=0 same 0.20 vs diff 0.00; theta=1.25 same 0.287 vs diff 0.00; margin/spread better at 128 than 64), and the causality-to-1e-6 claim reproduces exactly; the single 0.973 pointer figure is a favourable draw against a 0.87 mean, which is a reporting nit rather than a fabrication. Smaller overstatements: the prediction is not itself a convex combination of candidates (only the pre-readout mixture is), the cost quote says [B,64,n_steps] where the state is [B,128,n_steps], the "no observation value enters any gate" line is literally false since h_cmd carries earlier observations (the property that matters — the read's own observation being irrelevant — I verified as exactly 0.0), and the occlusion regulariser is bypassed by the inherited head, which reads un-occluded observations into the same prediction.

divergences.claim: "Depth-invariant composition. Because the transported value is renormalised back onto the simplex at every hop, a depth-4 chain is a product of four near-stochastic updates and the surviving pointer is as sharp as after one hop." Backed by an offline sim reporting 0.973 normalised mass on the true origin after a depth-3 chain with "essentially no attenuation with depth".
divergences.what_the_code_does: Depth-invariance holds only for the idealised address set their sim used (mutually near-orthogonal random unit vectors), not for the addresses this genome actually produces. Driving the real `_pointer_route` with addresses from the real `_role_addresses` on the real stream code (same N(0,1) unit-variance background their own second sim assumes), with IDEAL gates, the pointer's mass on the true origin falls with depth instead of staying flat. The degradation lands exactly on the eligible slice (depths 3 and 4).
divergences.evidence: Reproduced their sim first: 8 random unit addresses, 12 steps, ideal gates -> mean normalised mass on the true origin 0.87 at ptr_key_d=128 over 20 draws (their 0.973 is a favourable single draw; mean total mass 1.02, so "no attenuation" is right). A clean chain with only orthogonal-ish addresses is depth-flat: depth 1..6 all give mass-on-origin 1.000. Then the same recurrence with addresses built by net._role_addresses() from evolve.chunks.stream.r3_srcdst_hashslot_coding._sparse_block codes on an N(0,1) background, 30 seeds, ideal gates (g_move=1 on mv, 0 on cat; g_write=g_erase=1): N=8 slots -> depth 1: argmax==true-origin 57%, mass 0.354; depth 3: 20%, 0.171; depth 4: 23%, 0.154. N=4 slots -> depth 1: 60%/0.479; depth 3: 47%/0.330; depth 4: 20%/0.249. The reason is visible in their own second sim, which I also reproduced: same-path src/dst address cosine is only ~0.29, not ~1.0. Scripts: /tmp/rev21/t6.py, /tmp/rev21/t7.py, /tmp/rev21/t10.py. Mitigation not verifiable here: addr_proj and addr_thresh_raw are trainable, so training could sharpen the addresses; the claim as written is about the mechanism, and as a property of the mechanism at its shipped configuration it is false.

divergences.claim: "The learned power sharpening can additionally re-concentrate mass after each hop; nothing in a content store can do that." (offered as the mechanism's own remedy for cross-talk / diffuse reads)
divergences.what_the_code_does: The capability exists but cannot engage during a scored run. `self.ptr_log_sharp = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(-6.0))` and `_sharp_exponent = (1 + softplus(ptr_log_sharp)).clamp(1, 4)` start the exponent at 1.0025, i.e. sharpening off. The scalar routes to AdamW (ndim==0, not Muon, not the spectral cap), whose per-step displacement is bounded by roughly the lr, and the genome's optim schedule integrates to sum(lambda)=2667 at 4000 steps with lr=5e-4 -> total possible movement ~1.33, i.e. raw >= -4.67, exponent <= ~1.009.
divergences.evidence: Measured grad norm on ptr_log_sharp after one backward: 5.4e-07 (softplus Jacobian sigmoid(-6)=0.0025). Schedule integral via evolve.chunks.optim.r18_spectral_capped_transition_readout._schedule_lambda(4000, 0.04, 0.30, 0.05) = 2666.98; 5e-4 * 2666.98 = 1.333; softplus(-4.667) = 0.0094 -> exponent 1.009. Setting the exponent by hand shows what is being forfeited: on the real-address depth sim (N=8), exponent 1.002 -> depth 4 argmax 23%; exponent 2 -> 30%; exponent 4 -> 43%. So sharpening does what they say, and the shipped init puts it out of reach. Scripts: /tmp/rev21/t3.py, /tmp/rev21/t11.py.

divergences.claim: "Verbatim retrieval. The predicted content is always a convex combination of observation embeddings that actually occurred in this window ... so if the routing is right the prediction lands on the real content vector rather than near it."
divergences.what_the_code_does: What is always a convex combination is the intermediate `copy = p_norm @ obs_pad`. The prediction is `pred_trunk + sigmoid(ptr_gate) * ptr_out(copy)`, where ptr_out is a free (D,D) map initialised to 0.05*I and pred_trunk is the inherited trunk's competing output. The final prediction is not a convex combination of the candidate bank, and at init the injected term is ~0.6% of the prediction magnitude.
divergences.evidence: Code lines 234-247 of arch__r25_simplex_pointer_routing_denoised.py. Measured init deviation from the parent's prediction at command positions: mean 0.00302, max 0.0226, against pred scale 0.4786 (/tmp/rev21 inline check). Partly self-disclosed in their failure mode 3, which correctly notes the mixture lives in raw standardized obs space while the loss lives in the ZCA-whitened space of zca_shrunk_target_whitening.

divergences.claim: DESCRIPTION and hypothesis line 70: "all gates are functions of the command token and the causal hidden state only, never of any observation value".
divergences.what_the_code_does: The gate input is `gi = cat([h_cmd, gelu(ptr_feat(cmd_raw))])`, and h_cmd is the trunk's causal hidden state at command positions, which is a function of all strictly earlier observation values. The literal statement is false; the property that actually matters is true.
divergences.evidence: Verified the operative property directly: constructing a batch with an observation slot after the read and flipping only that slot's key_pad (present vs withheld) changes the prediction at every command position by exactly 0.0 (/tmp/rev21/t8.py). Also verified perturbing obs_{r-1} by 100x changes only command r's prediction, all earlier commands 0.0 (/tmp/rev21/t2.py).

divergences.claim: COST: "n_steps iterations over a [B, 64, n_steps] state".
divergences.what_the_code_does: `mem = a_src.new_zeros(B, self.ptr_key_d, n_cmd)` with ptr_key_d defaulting to 128 (which the hypothesis elsewhere argues for deliberately, as wider than the trunk's key_d=64). The state is [B, 128, n_cmd], twice the quoted size. The comparative conclusion (cheaper than the trunk's [key_d, 768] content stores) still holds.
divergences.evidence: net.ptr_key_d == 128, net.key_d == 64 on the built genome; 128*32 = 4096 vs 64*768 = 49152.

divergences.claim: "Occlusion is a regulariser ... it removes the 'the answer looks like the recent content I can see' crutch."
divergences.what_the_code_does: Occlusion is applied at the top of the arch's forward, so the trunk and both of the arch's retrieval channels see occluded observations, as claimed. But the genome's head r2_dualaddress_move_transport wraps net.forward from outside and calls mod.run(tok_emb, types, key_pad) on the ORIGINAL un-occluded tensors, adding its own content-transport read to the same command-position prediction. A parallel un-occluded content channel therefore survives the regulariser (out_scale is zero-init but trainable).
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/head/r2_dualaddress_move_transport.py wrap()._forward calls orig_forward(tok_emb,...) then mod.run(tok_emb,...) with the same outer tok_emb; the arch's _occlude runs inside orig_forward and its effect does not propagate to the wrapper's local. Inherited from the parent, not authored here.
